source_text: Et Polycarpus autem non solum ab Apostolis edoctus, et conversatus cum multis ex eis qui Dominum nostrum viderunt ; sed etiam ab Apostolis in Asia, in ea que est Smyrnis Ecclesia constitutus Episcopus, quem et nos vidimus in prima nostra eetate, multum enim perseveravit, et valde senex gloriosissime et nobilissime martyrium faciens exivit de hac vita, heee docuit semper quie ab Apostolis didicerat, quee et Ecclesiz tradidit, et sola sunt vera. estimonium his perhibent que sunt in Asia ecclesi omnes, et qui usque adhuc successerunt Polycarpo: qui vir multo majoris auctoritatis, et fidelior veritatis est testis, quam Valentinus et Marcion, et reliqui qui sunt perversze sententiz. Is enim est qui sub Aniceto cum advenisset in urbem, multos ex his quos preediximus, hzereticos convertit in Ecclesiam Dei, unam et solam hane veritatem annuntians ab Apostolis percepisse se, quam et Keclesize tradidit. Et sunt qui audierunt eum®, quoniam Johannes Domini discipulus in Epheso iens lavari, cum vidisset intus Cerinthum, exsilierit de balneo non lotus, dicens, quod timeat ne balneum concidat, cum intus esset Cerinthus inimicus veritatis. Et ipse autem Polycarpus Marcioni aliquando occurrenti sibi, et dicenti, Cognoscis nos? respondit: Cognosco te primogenitum Satan. Tantum Apostoli et horum discipuli habuerunt timorem, Sut neque verbo tenus communicarent alicui eorum qui adulteraverant veritatem, quemadmodum et Paulus ait: Hareticum autem hominem post unam correptionem devita, sciens quoniam perversus est qui est talis, et est a semetipso damnatus, Est autem et epistola Polycarpi ad Philippenses scripta perfectissima, ex qua et characterem fidei ejus, et preedicationem veritatis, qui volunt et curam habent suz salutis, possunt discere. Sed et que est Ephesi ecclesia a Paulo quidem fundata, Johanne autem permanente apud eos usque ad Trajani tempora, testis est verus Apostolorum traditionis,
pass_a_gloss: And Polycarpus indeed was not only taught by the Apostles and conversed with many of those who saw our Lord, but also was constituted Bishop by the Apostles in Asia, in the Church that is in Smyrna, whom also we saw in our first age, for he persevered much and as a very old man gloriously and most nobly made a martyrdom, exiting this life, he always taught what he had learned from the Apostles, which things also the Church handed down, and these alone are true. Testimony to these things is borne by all the Churches that are in Asia and those who have succeeded Polycarpus up to now, who is a man of much greater authority and a more faithful witness to the truth than Valentinus and Marcion and the rest who are of perverse opinion. For he is the one who, when he came to the city under Anicetus, converted many of those heretics we mentioned before to the Church of God, announcing one and only this truth, which he perceived from the Apostles and handed down to the Church. And there are those who heard him, that John, the Lord's disciple, going to bathe in Ephesus, when he saw Cerinthus inside, jumped out of the bath unbathed, saying that he feared the bath would collapse, since Cerinthus, an enemy of the truth, was inside. And Polycarpus himself, when Marcion met him and said, 'Do you recognize us?', replied, 'I recognize you as the firstborn of Satan.' The Apostles and their disciples had so much fear that they would not even communicate with any of those who had corrupted the truth, just as Paul also says: 'But a heretical man, after one correction, avoid, knowing that he who is such is perverse and is self-condemned.' There is also a letter of Polycarpus to the Philippians, written most perfectly, from which those who want to and have care for their salvation can learn his character of faith and the preaching of the truth. But also the Church that is in Ephesus, founded by Paul, and with John remaining among them until the times of Trajan, is a true witness of the Apostles' tradition,

pass_b_english: Polycarp was not only taught by the Apostles and conversed with many who had seen our Lord, but was also appointed bishop by the Apostles in Asia, in the Church at Smyrna. We ourselves saw him in our early years; he persevered a long time and, as a very old man, gloriously and most nobly met his martyrdom and departed this life. He always taught what he had learned from the Apostles, which the Church also handed down, and these things alone are true. All the Churches in Asia bear witness to this, as do those who have succeeded Polycarp down to the present. He is a man of far greater authority and a more faithful witness to the truth than Valentinus, Marcion, and the rest who hold perverse opinions. For when he came to Rome under Anicetus, he converted many of the heretics previously mentioned to the Church of God, proclaiming the one truth he had received from the Apostles and handed down to the Church. There are those who heard that when John, the Lord's disciple, went to bathe in Ephesus and saw Cerinthus inside, he rushed out of the bathhouse unwashed, declaring he feared the building would collapse because Cerinthus, an enemy of the truth, was within. And Polycarp himself, when Marcion once met him and asked, 'Do you recognize us?' replied, 'I recognize you as the firstborn of Satan.' The Apostles and their disciples had such dread of corrupting the truth that they would not so much as speak with any who had adulterated it, just as Paul says: 'A heretical man, after one correction, avoid, knowing that such a person is perverse and self-condemned' (Titus 3:10-11). There is also a letter of Polycarp to the Philippians, written most perfectly, from which those who desire and care for their salvation can learn the character of his faith and the preaching of the truth. Moreover, the Church at Ephesus, founded by Paul and with John remaining among them until the time of Trajan, stands as a true witness to the Apostles' tradition.
